[1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[4] PLATFORM OPTIONS

The i.MX 93 applications processors family, part of the 
EdgeVerse™ portfolio platform, offers multiple SoCs with 
a scalable option to move up or down depending on the 
application needs. The different products in the i.MX 93 
family include capabilities such as an integrated NPU and 
the number of Cortex-A55 cores. Additionally, pin-to-pin 
compatibility is planned between i.MX 93 and future i.MX 9 
series product families.

BUILT-IN MCU
A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time-
critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the 
need for an external microcontroller in the system design. 
The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN 
FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for 
industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex 
M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power 
wake-word detection.
i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS

[3] The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages High flexibility based on the latest technologies WHITEPAPER  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 2 How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? 3 Module Designs i.MX 93 processor 5 Mainboard Design 7 Available modules/mainboards of the i.MX 93 processor from TQ 15 Additional Information 18 Content  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 3 The i.MX 93 processor How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[4] PLATFORM OPTIONS

The i.MX 93 applications processors family, part of the 
EdgeVerse™ portfolio platform, offers multiple SoCs with 
a scalable option to move up or down depending on the 
application needs. The different products in the i.MX 93 
family include capabilities such as an integrated NPU and 
the number of Cortex-A55 cores. Additionally, pin-to-pin 
compatibility is planned between i.MX 93 and future i.MX 9 
series product families.

rows.prompt: Write a clear, friendly email to a colleague introducing the NXP i.MX 95 for a new edge-AI product. Cover what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it suits edge inference. Ground the specifics in the datasheets.
rows.raw:
Hi [Colleague's Name],

I'd like to introduce the NXP i.MX 95 for our next edge-AI product. This is the first i.MX to support functional safety with a built-in Arm Cortex-M33 as a safety island, and it offers a rich set of peripherals targeting Industrial, IoT, and Automotive.

**Main features:**
- Up to 6x Arm Cortex-A55 cores at up to 1.8 GHz, 32 kB L1 instruction cache, 32 kB L1 data cache (per core, parity protected), 64 kB L2 cache (per core, ECC protected), and 512 kB L3 cache (shared across all cores, ECC protected).
- 1x Arm Cortex-M7 at up to 800 MHz, Arm v8-M supporting TrustZone-M, 512 kB TCM (instruction + data).
- 1x Arm Cortex-M33 at up to 333 MHz, Arm v8-M supporting TrustZone-M, 16 kB instruction cache + 16 kB data cache (ECC), 512 kB TCM (instruction + data).
- One x32 LPDDR interface (with inline ECC), operating at up to 6400 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode.
- 3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1).
- 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, 1x Octal SPI, including SPI NOR and SPI NAND memories.

**Neutron NPU:**
The i.MX 95 integrates a Neutron N3-1024S eIQ Neutron NPU, an on-chip hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads. It works in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural-network (NN) inference. The NPU does not support the i.MX 95 reference manual NPU domain diagram, but it includes an activation engine, buffers, a data canvas, a rescaler/shifter, and a weight decoder, and it supports a wide range of TFLite operators. The eIQ tooling generates an NPU-optimized model that can be integrated into an ML application running on the target device.

**Why it suits edge inference:**
- **Low power and high performance.** The CPU and NPU work together, and the NPU's dedicated hardware can run at high throughput with low power.
- **Rich peripheral set.** The wide range of interfaces (SD, SPI, I3C, SDIO) makes it easy to connect sensors, displays, and storage.
- **Safety and security.** The Cortex-M33 as a safety

Hi [Colleague's Name],

Excited to share the i.MX 95 with you. It's the right fit for our edge-AI product, and I'll explain why.

**What it is**
The i.MX 95 is a Cortex-A55 based applications processor with up to six cores at up to 1.8 GHz. It also has a Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M33. It's the first i.MX to support functional safety with a built-in Cortex-M33 safety island. It's built with NXP's Energy Flex architecture for Industrial, IoT and Automotive devices.

**The Neutron NPU**
The i.MX 95 has an eIQ® Neutron N3-1024S NPU. It provides efficient machine-learning workload processing in conjunction with the CPU, delivering higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference. The NPU manages MAC compute block throughput, optimizes weight arrangement, manages memory accesses, and provides rescaling, activation, and pooling functions.

**Why it suits edge inference**
- **Cortex-A55 cores** at up to 1.8 GHz and a Cortex-M7 give you both high-performance CPU compute and a small, low-power core.
- **Neuron NPU** handles the workloads that are computationally heavy, leaving the CPU free for logic, control, and decision-making.
- **NXP's Energy Flex architecture** optimizes performance and power.
- **Rich peripherals** and the i.MX 95's industrial-qualified variants make it well suited to industrial and commercial IoT applications.
- **Cortex-M33 safety island** adds functional safety for systems that need it.
- **LPDDR5** support at up to 6400MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode gives you fast memory.

**Datasheet details**
- **Memory:** 19 x 19 mm package with one x32 LPDDR interface (with inline ECC) operating at up to 6400MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode. The 15 x 15 mm package is rated at 4266 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4000 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode.
- **Connectivity:** 3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1), 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, 1x Octal SPI with support for SPI NOR and SPI NAND memories.
- **Safety:** Industrial, Extended Industrial and Automotive level qualification are offered.

The i.MX 95 is part of NXP's EdgeVerse™ portfolio of intelligent edge solutions

Subject: Introducing the i.MX 95 for edge AI

Hi [Colleague],

I'd like to share the i.MX 95 with you. It's a great fit for edge inference, with a small form factor, low power, and a Cortex-A55 CPU plus the first on-chip NPU in the i.MX 9 series.

**Product overview**
- Cortex-A55 MPCore platform: 6 cores, up to 1.8 GHz, 32 kB L1 cache per core, 64 kB L2 and 512 kB L3, fully 64-bit capable.
- Memory: 19 x 19 mm package with one x32 LPDDR interface (6400 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode), plus 3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1).
- A rich set of peripherals: 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, 1x Octal SPI.
- Built with NXP's Energy Flex architecture, targeting Industrial, IoT and Automotive.

**The Neutron NPU**
The i.MX 95 is the first i.MX device to carry the eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU. It is an on-chip hardware accelerator for machine-learning workloads, working in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference. Key points from the reference manual:

- **Architecture:** Activation engine, rescaler/shifter, weight decoder, buffers, control, and a data canvas. It provides activation functions and rescales, shifts, and pools MAC compute block results.
- **Memory:** The NPU has its own 1 MB SRAM (TCM), plus the ability to access system memory.
- **Optimization:** It manages weights, memory accesses, and decompresses compressed weights. The reference manual also notes that some features and operators may not be enabled in the eIQ software.
- **Software:** Enablement is provided with the eIQ Toolkit and eIQ Machine Learning Software Development Environment. You can import your trained and quantized NN into the toolkit, which generates an NPU-optimized model that can be integrated into an ML application on the target device.

**Why it suits edge inference**
1. **Low power and small size.** The i.MX 95 is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series, and the Neutron NPU is efficient in both memory and power.
2. **Built-in hardware acceleration.** The CPU plus NPU are designed to work together, so you can offload work from the CPU.
3. **Rich peripheral set.** The I/O and memory options

claims: Subject: Introducing the i.MX 95 for edge AI
I'd like to share the i.MX 95 with you.
It's a great fit for edge inference, with a small form factor, low power, and a Cortex-A55 CPU plus the first on-chip NPU in the i.MX 9 series.
Cortex-A55 MPCore platform: 6 cores, up to 1.8 GHz, 32 kB L1 cache per core, 64 kB L2 and 512 kB L3, fully 64-bit capable.
Memory: 19 x 19 mm package with one x32 LPDDR interface (6400 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode or 4266 MT/s in LPDDR4X mode), plus 3x uSDHC (SD3.0, SDIO3.0, eMMC5.1).
A rich set of peripherals: 8x LPI2C, 8x LPSPI, 2x I3C, 1x Octal SPI.
Built with NXP's Energy Flex architecture, targeting Industrial, IoT and Automotive.
The i.MX 95 is the first i.MX device to carry the eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU.
It is an on-chip hardware accelerator for machine-learning workloads, working in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference.
Architecture:** Activation engine, rescaler/shifter, weight decoder, buffers, control, and a data canvas.
It provides activation functions and rescales, shifts, and pools MAC compute block results.
Memory:** The NPU has its own 1 MB SRAM (TCM), plus the ability to access system memory.
Optimization:** It manages weights, memory accesses, and decompresses compressed weights.
The reference manual also notes that some features and operators may not be enabled in the eIQ software.
Software:** Enablement is provided with the eIQ Toolkit and eIQ Machine Learning Software Development Environment.
You can import your trained and quantized NN into the toolkit, which generates an NPU-optimized model that can be integrated into an ML application on the target device.
Low power and small size.** The i.MX 95 is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series, and the Neutron NPU is efficient in both memory and power.
Built-in hardware acceleration.** The CPU plus NPU are designed to work together, so you can offload work from the CPU.
Rich peripheral set.** The I/O and memory options

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The Neutron N3-1024S NPU is an on-chip hardware accelerator that processes machine-learning workloads, working with the chip's CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network inference. Key features, from the i.MX 95 Reference Manual, include:

- **Convolutional neural networks (CNN)**: support for 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, and 7x7 convolutions with stride and padding, as well as 1x3, 3x1, 1x5, 5x1, 1x7, and 7x1 variants. The manual also lists support for atrous separable convolution networks and depthwise separable convolutional networks.
- **Recurrent neural networks (RNN)**: including minimum gated unit (MGU) networks.
- **Activation functions**: ReLu, PreLu, LeakyReLu.
- **Sampling or reshaping functions** and **element-wise operations**.
- **Layer operations** and **normalization

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The Neutron N3-1024S NPU in the i.MX 95 is a hardware accelerator that processes machine-learning workloads. It works with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural-network (NN) inference. Its key features, per the reference manual, include:

- 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz, with a 2 OPS/MAC throughput.
- 1 MB local SRAM.
- Natively supporting CNNs including Atrous Separable Convolution and Depthwise Separable Convolutional networks, with matrix sizes of 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, 7x7, 1x3, 3x1, 1x5, 5x1, 1x7, and 7x1, plus stride and padding support.
- Recurrent Neural Networks including minimum gated unit (MGU) networks.
- Activation function support for ReLu, PreLu, LeakyReLu.
- Sampling or resh

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The i.MX 95 NPU is a hardware accelerator for machine learning (ML) workloads. It works in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference.

Key features (from the i.MX 95 Reference Manual):
- 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC.
- 1 MB local SRAM.
- Native support for convolutional neural networks (CNN), including Atrous Separable Convolution networks and Depthwise Separable Convolutional networks, with matrix sizes of 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, and 7x7 (with stride and padding support) and 1x3, 3x1, 1x5, 5x1, 1x7, and 7x1.
- Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), including minimum gated unit (MGU) networks.
- Activation function support, including ReLu, PreLu, and LeakyRe

rows.raw:
**NXP i.MX 95 Overview**
A Cortex-A55-based applications processor with 16-bit memory interface, supporting LPDDR4/4X with internal ECC. Four processing pipeline variants (1-4 cores) with optional NPU, qualified over a wide temperature range. Up to 4K resolution at 30 fps, 2K at 30 or 60 fps per channel, and stream multiplexing from a single 4-lane MIPI input.

**NPU**
eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU, Neuron 4 cores, provides efficient machine-learning processing, including weight decompression, rescaling, activation, and pooling. It works with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power for neural network inference.

**Memory/Connectivity**
- Memory map: Cortex-M7, Cortex-M33, and Cortex-A55 regions, OCRAM, and LPDDR4/4X (up to 1.7 GHz A55).
- Connectivity: 2x CAN-FD, 2x FlexIO, 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1 with TSN), 2x USB 2.0, 4x I2S, 8x UART, 8x SPI, 8x I2C, 2x I3C, 2x ADC (4-channel, 12-bit), 2x PDM microphone input, 1x Arm Neon FPU, 256 kB L2 cache, and 16-bit parallel RGB display interface.
- Security: Secure clock, secure boot, battery-backed secure module (BBSM) domain, and sensors/tamper detection.

**Target Markets**
- Industrial automation, machine vision, and edge AI applications where small form factor, long-term supply, and low power are key. The 15-year supply longevity program and the 16-bit pixel link crossbar make it suitable for cameras, sensors, and display-driven systems where performance and security matter.

claims: A Cortex-A55-based applications processor with 16-bit memory interface, supporting LPDDR4/4X with internal ECC.
Four processing pipeline variants (1-4 cores) with optional NPU, qualified over a wide temperature range.
Up to 4K resolution at 30 fps, 2K at 30 or 60 fps per channel, and stream multiplexing from a single 4-lane MIPI input.
eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU, Neuron 4 cores, provides efficient machine-learning processing, including weight decompression, rescaling, activation, and pooling.
It works with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power for neural network inference.
Memory map: Cortex-M7, Cortex-M33, and Cortex-A55 regions, OCRAM, and LPDDR4/4X (up to 1.7 GHz A55).

Connectivity: 2x CAN-FD, 2x FlexIO, 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1 with TSN), 2x USB 2.0, 4x I2S, 8x UART, 8x SPI, 8x I2C, 2x I3C, 2x ADC (4-channel, 12-bit), 2x PDM microphone input, 1x Arm Neon FPU, 256 kB L2 cache, and 16-bit parallel RGB display interface.
Security: Secure clock, secure boot, battery-backed secure module (BBSM) domain, and sensors/tamper detection.
Industrial automation, machine vision, and edge AI applications where small form factor, long-term supply, and low power are key.
The 15-year supply longevity program and the 16-bit pixel link crossbar make it suitable for cameras, sensors, and display-driven systems where performance and security matter.

rows.raw:
**NXP i.MX 95 Overview**
- Multi-core SoC with Cortex-A55 CPU, Cortex-M7 and Cortex-M33 cores
- 2x 4-lane or 1x 8-lane LVDS, 2x 1 GbE (w/TSN), 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE (w/TSN) and 3x SD/eMMC5.1
- 1492kB OCRAM (ECC), 512kB TCM (ECC), 64kB L2 cache, 32kB i-cache, 32kB d-cache
- Arm Mali 3D GPU and 2D GPU, image signal processor, 2x MIPI-CSI 4-lane, 1x MIPI-DSI 4-lane (w/PHY)
- eIQ® Neutron N3-1024S NPU for efficient machine-learning workloads
- Industrial-grade temperature and extended temperature variants, and 2-year support

**NPU (Neutron N3-1024S)**
- 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz, with 2 OPS/MAC
- 1 MB local SRAM, 2.0 TOP/s performance
- Supports CNN (Atrous Separable Convolution, Depthwise Separable Convolutional networks), RNN (MGU networks), and activation functions (ReLU, PreLu, LeakyReLu), sampling/reshaping, element-wise, layer, normalization and pooling functions
- Optional interrupt on memory error events, and error event capturing for memory sources

**Memory & Connectivity**
- LPDDR5/LPDDR4X (Inline ECC & Encryption)
- 2x 4-lane or 1x 8-lane LVDS, 2x 1 GbE (w/TSN), 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE (w/TSN)
- 3x SD/eMMC5.1, Octal SPI flash (inline crypto), XSPI responder, 4K Video Processing Unit

**Target Markets**
- Industrial and IoT applications, where machine learning and intelligent edge processing are proliferating
- The i.MX 95 is targeted at a range of industrial and IoT devices such as factory automation, building automation, smart energy and smart home, and smart city, where low energy consumption, reduced resource usage and waste, and intelligent edge and machine learning are key.

This translation is based on address mapping and memory attribute information that is available from configuration tables and translation tables that are stored in memory. SMMU can support up to two stages of translation: • One TCU in NoC domain • Three TBUs in Wakeup domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC0) in Wakeup domain • Eight TBUs in NoC domain • One DTI interconnect (DTI_IC1) in NoC domain • Two AXI-4 Stream SSIs for the DTI interface between Wakeup domain: DTI_IC0 and NoC domain DTI_IC1 • SMMU performs translation table walks for each stage of translation and supports up to 48 bit VA (virtual address). • SMMU TTB1 table must be disabled using EPD1 (disable) fields in the Context Descriptor for the existence of TTB1 table. Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.
